records.summary: Act No. 442/2000 Coll. amended the Czech National Bank Act (Act No. 6/1993 Coll.) so that the government, rather than the bank or the President alone, would propose the candidates for Governor and Vice-Governors; the Constitutional Court's judgment Pl. US 14/01 of 20 June 2001 records that this paragraph 6(3) was later annulled by its judgment Pl. US 278/2000, and states that the independence of the CNB is a constitutional value and that in safeguarding its main goals the CNB is independent of instructions from the government. Separate from the 2015 presidential pressure episode already on the map.
records.source_title: Constitutional Court of the Czech Republic, judgment of 20 June 2001, Pl. US 14/01 (Czech National Bank)

records.summary: The Swiss federal parliament's Parliamentary Investigation Committee (PUK/PInC), set up on 8 June 2023 and reporting on 20 December 2024, examined the conduct of the authorities in the emergency takeover of Credit Suisse, and its inquiry expressly covered the Swiss National Bank alongside the Federal Council, the Federal Department of Finance, FINMA and the Federal Audit Oversight Authority. The committee found the informal autumn 2022 meetings initiated by the then finance minister and the Chairman of the SNB's Governing Board to be of limited use because they were not sufficiently coordinated within the regular crisis structures. This is a parliamentary inquiry into the bank, distinct from the 2012 Hildebrand resignation already on the map.
records.source_title: Swiss Parliament press release, 'Parliamentary committee calls for lessons to be learned from the emergency merger of CS and UBS', 20 December 2024

records.kind: law change the bank objected to in writing
records.summary: Banka Slovenije publicly warned the National Assembly, in a statement of 16 October 2019 issued before the vote, that the bill on judicial protection of former holders of qualified bank claims contained provisions it could not accept: an obligation on the central bank to pay flat-rate compensation to certain holders, which it said was disputable primarily on the grounds of the prohibition of monetary financing, and a liability regime it described as potentially objective with a reversed burden of proof, which it called exceptional for public institutions in Slovenia and the EU. The bank said the bill encroached on a fundamental principle of the functioning of central banks in the euro area. Distinct from the 2016 search of the bank's premises already on the map.
records.source_title: Banka Slovenije, 'Regulation of judicial relief for holders of subordinated debt: Bank of Slovenia again warns of disputed provisions before voting', 16 October 2019

records.summary: The government moved to remove State Bank of Pakistan governor Tariq Bajwa on Friday 3 May 2019, together with the chairman of the Federal Board of Revenue; Bajwa confirmed to Dawn that he was asked to resign, no official reason was given for the removals, and a letter of resignation was still required before his departure took effect. He was replaced within days by an IMF economist. Distinct from the 2014 governor's resignation and the 2023 Public Accounts Committee audit direction already on the map.
records.source_title: Dawn, 'SBP governor, FBR chairman shown the door', 4 May 2019

records.kind: central bank law put under government-ordered review
records.summary: Terms of reference published by the Australian Treasury on 20 July 2022 put the Reserve Bank of Australia's own statutory objectives under external review, directing the reviewers to assess the RBA's objectives as set out in the Reserve Bank Act 1959, including the continued appropriateness of the inflation targeting framework, the bank's governance including board structure, composition, expertise and the appointments process, its accountability arrangements, and its culture, management and recruitment processes, with a final report of recommendations to go to the Treasurer by March 2023. Distinct from the July 2023 public pressure episode already on the map.
records.source_title: Australian Treasury, 'Reserve Bank of Australia review - Terms of reference', 20 July 2022

records.summary: On 7 April 2016 the governing Saenuri Party announced a package including a revision of the Bank of Korea Act that would, in its own description, enable the party to demand the central bank introduce quantitative easing, with the Bank of Korea supplying more liquidity by buying bonds issued by state-run banks, among them the state-owned Korea Development Bank, and commercial banks' mortgage-backed securities; the party said it would table the revision within 100 days of the new National Assembly convening on 30 May, and a senior party official dismissed concerns that it would violate the central bank's independent decision-making. Distinct from the 2014 public pressure episode already on the map.
records.source_title: The Korea Times, 'Saenuri seeks to revise BOK law for pump-priming', 7 April 2016

records.summary: Georgia's parliament passed, on an expedited basis, amendments to the law governing the National Bank of Georgia that would let a newly created special representative stand in for the bank's president in his absence and would increase the number of executive board members; the National Bank itself said in early February 2023 that the changes threatened its independence and that its activities had never been affected by the absence of its president, and President Salome Zourabichvili vetoed the amendments on 23 February 2023 as neither necessary, urgent nor reasoned, noting the stand-in could act for an indefinite period. Distinct from the 2015 law change already on the map.
records.source_title: bne IntelliNews, 'Georgian president vetoes National Bank amendments', February 2023

records.summary: A first draft revision of the 1999 Bank Indonesia law, presented to the legislative committee of Indonesia's House of Representatives and reported on 1 September 2020, would create a monetary council chaired by the finance minister to lead, coordinate and direct monetary policy in line with the government's general policy, seat the coordinating economic affairs minister and the OJK chairman alongside the governor and senior deputy governor on a five-member board meeting twice a month, make permanent the bank's purchases of government bonds in the primary market, and return banking supervision to the bank; a deputy chair of the committee said lawmakers wanted to rein in the bank's independence. Distinct from the 2000 prosecution already on the map.
records.source_title: The Jakarta Post, 'House mulls fundamental changes to how Bank Indonesia operates', 1 September 2020

records.summary: A bill initiated by Liviu Dragnea and Serban Nicolae, already adopted by the Senate, would have obliged the National Bank of Romania to repatriate 91.5 per cent of the gold it holds abroad, about 56 tonnes, and a commission amendment would have required the bank to inform Parliament and the Government within 20 days of any crisis endangering monetary stability; at the Chamber of Deputies budget, finance and banking commission on 19 April 2019 the bank stated through a senior expert that it could not back the proposal in the form adopted by the Senate, rejected the senator's further amendments, and argued that decisions on holding and administering international reserves rest with the national central bank under EU law. Distinct from the February 2019 asset-tax episode already on the map.
records.source_title: ActMedia, 'BNR: We can not support the legislative proposal on repatriation of gold', 19 April 2019

records.summary: Tunisia's Assembly of the Representatives of the People adopted, by 92 votes to 15 with 26 abstentions at a sitting reported on 7 February 2024, a bill exceptionally authorising the Central Bank of Tunisia to grant 7 billion dinars to the general treasury; the government of President Kais Saied had asked parliament in late January 2024 to let the bank buy up to 7 billion dinars of interest-free government bonds to help close a 10 billion dinar budget deficit, after parliament had already revised laws meant to guarantee the bank's autonomy. Distinct from the 2012 dismissal of the governor already on the map.
records.source_title: Managers.tn, 'Adoption du projet de loi autorisant exceptionnellement la BCT a octroyer 7 milliards de dinars a la Tresorerie generale', 7 February 2024

blanks.note: Candidate second episode: the resignation of Bank Negara Malaysia governor Muhammad Ibrahim on 6 June 2018, a month after Finance Minister Lim Guan Eng revealed that the bank's purchase of government land had funded a 1MDB obligation. Free Malaysia Today, 'BNM governor resigns' (6 June 2018, freemalaysiatoday.com/category/nation/2018/06/06/bnm-governor-resigns), read in full: Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad confirmed the resignation after Cabinet and said the governor gave no concrete reason and only expressed his desire to resign, and that there was no mention of the land deals when the resignation was tendered. The article links the exit to Lim's revelation by timing only and does not say the minister or government sought it. Refused under the rule that an unexplained early exit with no source stating pressure is not this row. A source in which a state organ states a ground would convert it. The map's existing MYS record is the 1998 resignation under pressure.

Beyond the PUK record filed above, the 20 December 2024 Swiss Parliament press release on the PUK final report was read in full for further SNB-specific findings: apart from the finding on the autumn 2022 informal meetings, the criticisms (information flow, coordination, the then finance minister Ueli Maurer) are addressed to the authorities collectively or to the Federal Council and FINMA, and the committee found no misconduct by the authorities as a causative factor. The full PUK report itself (hundreds of pages, not opened here) is the next document for this country and may carry SNB-specific findings the press release does not.

The intellinews report of the presidential veto does not say whether parliament overrode it, so the record above is filed as an attempted law change. A search result not opened for budget reasons (sakartvelosambebi.ge, 'Parliament overrides president's veto on law on the National Bank') suggests the veto was overridden and the amendments entered force; if a next round confirms that on the parliament's own site, the record should be re-kinded to a law change and the appointment of Natia Turnava as acting governor under it added.

Neither source opened (africanews 1 February 2024; managers.tn 7 February 2024) states which article of the 2016 Central Bank of Tunisia law the 2024 authorisation derogates from, and neither carries any statement by the Central Bank of Tunisia or its governor objecting. The record above therefore rests on the parliamentary vote and the government's request, not on a written objection by the bank. The BCT's own communiques and the Journal Officiel text of the February 2024 law are the documents that would supply both.

leads_not_opened.note: Lebanon holds only the 2024 arrest of Riad Salameh. The 2020-2022 judicial and state actions against the Banque du Liban itself (the government-ordered forensic audit the bank initially refused to supply data for; the judicial seizure of bank records) are a separate episode family and were not searched this round.

Uganda holds only the 2018 COSASE probe. Parliament's 2024-2025 examination of the Bank of Uganda following the theft of about USD 62m from its accounts is a possible second parliamentary inquiry, but was not opened; care is needed because the bank is the victim of the theft itself.

Taiwan's Control Yuan publishes corrective measures and censures against audited state bodies and is the supreme-audit-institution vein for this country; Chinese-language only and not opened for budget reasons.
Iraq holds only the 2012 dismissal of Sinan al-Shabibi. Later parliamentary summonses of Central Bank of Iraq governors over the dinar and the currency auction were not searched.
